name: Linear seating arrangement
statement: \text{Fix the most definite clue first, draw the seats, place the rest clue by clue, and flip left/right for people facing south.}
derivation: Draw the seats as blanks numbered left to right (as the sitters face north).
Place definite clues first: 'R sits in the middle', 'T sits at an end'.
Add relative clues next ('P immediately left of R'); branch into cases when a clue allows two seats.
Kill cases using negative clues ('Q is not next to P') until one arrangement is left.
For people facing south, their left is your right on the paper.
visual_proof: A row of five boxes facing north, filled in clue order: R in the middle, P left of R, T at the end, Q away from P, S in the last gap.
common_traps: Using your own left for a sitter facing south.
Reading 'immediately left' as 'somewhere to the left'.
Not checking the second case of a two-way clue (T at either end).
Answering before every clue has been used.

diagram.alt_text: Five seats in a row facing north, left to right: S, P, R, Q, T. S sits at the extreme left.

verification.code:
from itertools import permutations

def arrangements(people, clues):
    """Rows facing north, seats listed left to right (the sitters' own left)."""
    return [row for row in permutations(people) if all(c(row) for c in clues)]

pos = lambda row, x: row.index(x)
# Constructed: P, Q, R, S, T sit in a row facing north.
clues = [
    lambda r: pos(r, "R") == 2,                          # R sits in the middle
    lambda r: pos(r, "P") == pos(r, "R") - 1,            # P is immediately left of R
    lambda r: pos(r, "T") in (0, 4),                     # T sits at an end
    lambda r: abs(pos(r, "Q") - pos(r, "P")) > 1,        # Q is not next to P
    lambda r: pos(r, "S") < pos(r, "T"),                 # S is somewhere left of T
]
res = arrangements("PQRST", clues)
assert res == [tuple("SPRQT")], res
options = {"A": "P", "B": "T", "C": "S", "D": "Q"}
assert [k for k, v in options.items() if v == res[0][0]] == ["C"]       # extreme left: S

# Facing south flips left and right: 'P immediately left of R' then means P is one seat east of R.
def left_of(row, a, b, facing):
    return pos(row, a) == pos(row, b) + (-1 if facing == "north" else 1)
row = tuple("SPRQT")                                     # written west to east
assert left_of(row, "P", "R", "north") and not left_of(row, "P", "R", "south")
assert left_of(row, "Q", "R", "south")

name: Circular seating arrangement
statement: \text{Fix one person, then place the rest relative to fixed seats; facing the centre, right = anticlockwise, facing outward it flips.}
derivation: Fix any one person's seat; rotations of the whole table are the same arrangement.
Facing the centre: the person to your right is the next seat anticlockwise; to your left, clockwise.
Facing outward the two sides swap; opposite seats are the same either way.
Place definite clues, branch for two-way clues, and eliminate with negative clues.
visual_proof: A round table with A fixed at the bottom; everyone faces inward, so moving anticlockwise is moving to each person's right.
common_traps: Using right = clockwise for people facing the centre.
Not flipping left/right for people facing outward.
Counting 'second to the left' as two seats from your own seat on the paper, not the sitter's left.
Fixing two people independently and counting a rotation as a new arrangement.

diagram.alt_text: Six people round a table facing the centre, in anticlockwise order A, B, C, D, E, F. B is on A's right, D is opposite A, C is on D's left, and C is second to the left of E.

verification.code:
from itertools import permutations

N = 6
def seats(order):
    """order[i] = person in seat i; seats numbered anticlockwise seen from above."""
    return {p: i for i, p in enumerate(order)}

def right_of(s, x, k=1, facing="centre"):
    """Who sits k places to x's right. Facing the centre, right = anticlockwise; facing out it flips."""
    step = k if facing == "centre" else -k
    return (s[x] + step) % N

def arrangements(people, clues):
    first, rest = people[0], people[1:]
    out = []
    for p in permutations(rest):                         # fix the first person: no rotations repeated
        order = (first,) + p
        s = seats(order)
        if all(c(s) for c in clues):
            out.append(order)
    return out

# Constructed: A-F around a circular table facing the centre.
clues = [
    lambda s: s["B"] == right_of(s, "A"),                # B is immediately right of A
    lambda s: s["D"] == right_of(s, "A", 3),             # D is opposite A
    lambda s: s["C"] == right_of(s, "D", -1),            # C is immediately left of D
    lambda s: (s["F"] - s["D"]) % N not in (1, N - 1),   # F is not next to D
]
res = arrangements("ABCDEF", clues)
assert len(res) == 1, res
s = seats(res[0])
inv = {v: k for k, v in s.items()}
second_left_of_e = inv[right_of(s, "E", -2)]
assert second_left_of_e == "C"
options = {"A": "B", "B": "C", "C": "F", "D": "D"}
assert [k for k, v in options.items() if v == second_left_of_e] == ["B"]

# Facing outward flips the sides: the person on A's right when facing in is on A's left when facing out.
assert right_of(s, "A", 1, "centre") == right_of(s, "A", -1, "out")
# Opposite seat is the same either way
assert right_of(s, "A", 3, "centre") == right_of(s, "A", 3, "out")
